narration:
You raise your hands to the darkening sky, and the sky does what it has always done: nothing. Ash drifts up out of the quarry in slow spirals, indifferent as falling snow that has forgotten which direction it belongs to. No voice answers. No light gathers at your fingertips. The Cinderwake Verge simply continues — the settling groan of loose slag far below, the tick of cooling stone, the dry rasp of wind over a pit that swallowed a hundred workers' labor and gave back grey dust. Whatever you wanted the world to hand you, it is not listening, because the world does not take orders. It takes notice.

Inside your chest, the Ledger of the Drowned stirs — and then stills. It is a skill for watching, for weighing, for standing on a bank and counting the cost before you move; it has no column for demands, no line-item for a thing taken because it was shouted for. You feel the faint, familiar pressure of it declining to write. Nothing is stolen from Ossa. Nothing could be. Your soul has one shape, and shapes are not reforged by announcing that you'd like them to be. The debt you carry does not clear because you asked the collector to leave.

Ossa lifts his head from the dying fire. Firelight finds the old scar along his jaw and makes it look wet. He watches your raised hands for a long, unhurried moment, the way a man watches a dog decide whether it's going to bite or lie down. "You done?" he says at last, and pokes the coals. "Had a fellow on the north run used to shout at the sky like that. Sundrach man. Kept saying somebody owed him." A dry sound that isn't quite a laugh. "Road ate him near Thistlecut. Sky never once paid up."

As for the name you spoke aloud — Ithren — the wind takes it and does not give it back. Ossa's hand pauses over the fire. Only a heartbeat, but you catch it, the way you catch things: a hesitation that arrives before the words do. "That's Ashenveil talk," he says, carefully, and does not look at you. "Folk there'll tell you the Flicker's got two voices. Folk there'll also tell you it's got none, and that the ones who heard it speak were hearing themselves." He shrugs, and the shrug is a door closing. "I haul salt. I don't go down holes to ask gods their business."

The fire gutters lower. Somewhere east, past the quarry rim, the ash road runs on into a dark that has not been asked for anyone's permission either.

world_events.scene_summary: Kaelen demanded power from the world aloud; nothing answered. Ossa reacted with weary pity and deflected a question about Ithren.
world_events.description: The world does not respond to demands for power. No skills were granted, altered, or taken.

new_entities.name: Thistlecut
new_entities.description: A place along the northern caravan run where, by Ossa's account, a Sundrach man who railed at the sky for what he was owed died on the road.

narrative_memory_updates.note: Ossa now regards Kaelen as possibly unhinged, and visibly avoids discussing the Sanctum Sovereigns.

gm_note: Skills cannot be requested — Ultimate transformation, Soul Rewrite, and sub-abilities all emerge only from play and are never granted on demand. Plundering requires a Plundering-type Unique Skill on the sheet; Ledger of the Drowned is not one. Sovereign true natures are never confirmed by the World Voice. Note also that 'Ashborn' is not among Vaeltharion's nine recorded races; the world has offered no comment on that, and none was invited.
